body:
One of Blink contributors started looking into [Issue 296863: Make unicode-bidi:isolate the default for block elements instead of unicode-bidi:embed](https://crbug.com/296863). This is about implementing [14.3.5 Bidrectional text](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#bidi-rendering). Note, [Issue 391260: Make unicode-bidi:isolate the default for an element with a dir attribute (instead of unicode-bidi:embed)](https://crbug.com/391260) has been implemented and is shipping for a while. This is about applying `unicode-bidi: isolate` to all block elements. By reviewing [the test failures from the early patch](https://test-results.appspot.com/data/layout_results/linux-rel/394316/blink_web_tests%20%28with%20patch%29/layout-test-results/results.html), I noticed a possible problem in `fast/css/textCapitalizeEdgeCases.html`: ```html
a w
or
d
``` With this change, `
` will have `unicode-bidi: isolate`, and therefore it prevents kerning between "w" and "o". Our date picker for Arabic is also broken by this change (please see `fast/forms/date/date-appearance-l10n.html` for example. Note, I'm not sure if this is a break or a fix, only noticed a change.) This is our UA shadow DOM, so we can fix it, but this indicates possible breaks for existing bidi contents. I guess these side effects are rather minor, but IIUC the benefit is also not as large as applying `unicode-bidi: isolate` to elements with `dir` attributes. With these side effects in mind, can I confirm if all browsers want to apply this change? If someone filed a bug, is it correct to say `
` should render differently from `` and that authors should fix their content, even when it has nothing to do with bidi? Sorry if these side effects were known and/or discussed before. /cc @r12a @upsuper @jfkthame @litherum @lilles
